clue.text: Left-wing politician holds accountant in the gulag

indicators.note: the politician's title grips the accountant's letters between its two parts

parts.note: a Labour MP sits for Britain's left-of-centre Labour Party
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A socialist MP is keeping a bookkeeper prisoner in a Soviet camp.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulag was the Soviet system of forced-work prisons, so a prison of this kind is one example.

clue.text: Spike is fifty-one

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A sharp point is said to be numbered fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' here is a verb: to spike a drink is to add alcohol to it secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean secretly adding spirits or a drug to someone's drink.

clue.text: Abusive onslaught from a vulgar group of players

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team of coarse players delivers a stream of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a volley of all a warship's guns becomes a fierce verbal attack.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready to go, despite disturbance

parts.note: someone up has got out of bed
set means prepared, as in 'ready, set, go'

explanation.surface: Someone is awake and prepared to leave despite some commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval or upsetting event is a disturbance, a noun sense.

clue.text: Succeeded-but not at riding a bicycle

definitions.text: but not at riding a bicycle

explanation.surface: Something worked out well, though a cycling lesson went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: on a bicycle, to do this is to fall off rather than succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that worked has turned out well; a cyclist who tumbles from the saddle has fallen off.

clue.text: Milliner is the first to be in fashion

indicators.note: the letters of 'is' plus the first of 'the' are placed inside the fashion word

parts.note: mode is a fashion or style
taken as written

indicators.note: 'the first' asks for the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A hat maker claims to be the earliest to follow a trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' gives T, the opening letter of 'the'; 'in' places it, with the word is, inside the fashion word.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a maker of women's hats and dresses, so a hat maker fits.

clue.text: Special constable hesitates to answer the rabble

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer British police officer
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman falters when facing the mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous word for the lowest, most worthless people, the mob.

clue.text: Go first-class

explanation.surface: Two words: try something, and top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a crack is having a try or attempt; a crack shot is a top-grade expert one.

clue.text: Eton men, Sir, order soup

indicators.note: to order the letters is to rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boys from the famous school address a master and ask for a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: Middle-man enters to inform and evaluate

indicators.note: the central letter goes inside the word for informing

parts.note: to apprise someone is to inform them

indicators.note: the middle of 'man' is its central letter

explanation.surface: A go-between comes in to brief people and assess things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-man' looks like a go-between; it is A, the middle letter of 'man', entering APPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess or judge the worth of something is to evaluate it.

clue.text: Angry note to T E Lawrence

parts.note: C is a musical note
Lawrence of Arabia enlisted in the RAF under the assumed name John Hume Ross

explanation.surface: A furious message is sent to Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: T E Lawrence hid his fame by joining the RAF in 1922 as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is an informal synonym for annoyed or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Declared manufactured without adornment

parts.note: made means produced or manufactured
plain means simple, without decoration

explanation.surface: Something announced as being produced with no frills.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear or explicit is to state it openly, as a declaration does.

clue.text: It is done to produce copies of the paper

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a fresh product, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A printing works explains how newspapers come off the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Each print run of a newspaper is one issue, an edition of it.

clue.text: Roues used to pick up

explanation.surface: Debauched men employed to collect things.
explanation.definitionFit: A roue is a debauched man, a libertine; garden tools with teeth gather leaves.

clue.text: Dalmatian dessert

explanation.surface: A spotted breed of dog doubles as a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DOG is a British steamed suet pudding with currants, like spotted dick.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a dog with a speckled coat; a currant-studded suet pudding is a British sweet.

clue.text: Succeeded in getting a golden handshake

explanation.surface: Someone did well and was given a generous leaving package.
explanation.walkthrough: A golden handshake is a large payment to someone leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble that worked was rewarded; a dismissed worker settled with a cash sum was bought out.

clue.text: By the sound of it, supervises workers abroad

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the answer is spoken like another word

parts.note: a manager who oversees workers supervises them

explanation.surface: Apparently a manager directs staff in foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in a foreign country is living across the sea, away from home.

clue.text: One who turns out to be a key winner

parts.note: E is a musical key
a victor wins

explanation.surface: Someone proves to be a crucial champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns out' is not 'proves to be' but a phrasal verb: to throw someone out of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who removes tenants from a property is ousting them.

clue.text: Examine whether one press chief gave evidence

parts.note: to test is to examine
if means whether
I is the Roman numeral one
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Checking if a single newspaper editor spoke in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To give testimony under oath is to make a statement as a witness.

clue.text: He enters to negotiate on that account

indicators.note: the pronoun goes into the word for negotiating

parts.note: to treat with someone is to negotiate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man comes in to bargain for that reason.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning because of that, for that reason.

clue.text: Word I note to be of interest to the entomologist

parts.note: a term is a word
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A word and a note that should catch an insect scientist's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists study insects, and the termite is an insect.

clue.text: Go ahead and start the computer working

explanation.surface: Carry on and switch the machine on.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue determinedly is to proceed; to push a switch is to power a machine up.

clue.text: No-one retired is accommodated by noble colonist

indicators.note: the turned letters are taken in and housed by the noble's word

parts.note: a peer is a noble

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nobody withdrawn is housed by a lord who settled abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-one' looks like nobody; 'retired' turns NOI round to ION, and 'accommodated by' lodges that inside the noble after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Early settlers of new land were trailblazers opening it up.

clue.text: Those represented the prevailing attitudes

indicators.note: re-presented, the letters are set out again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Those views were the dominant ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a group is its characteristic spirit and beliefs.

clue.text: Pull up in the avenue

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words the avenue

explanation.surface: Stop in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' suggests stopping a car; it means haul upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to lift or haul with great effort.

clue.text: Figure emerging from house in strangely morbid surroundings

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form the surround with the house abbreviation within
strangely means the letters of morbid are set out oddly

explanation.surface: A shape appears from a home set in gloomy grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' gives RMBOID, and 'surroundings' makes it wrap the house abbreviation just after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomboid is a parallelogram with unequal sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Lifted up a large flat piece of wood

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the letters up reads them backwards

parts.note: a slab is a large flat piece of stone or wood

explanation.surface: A big plank of timber is hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted up' turns A SLAB to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber, used for models.

clue.text: The sixth age shifts into the-and slipper'd pantaloon."('As You Like It')

definitions.text: The sixth age shifts into the-and slipper'd pantaloon."('As You Like It')

parts.words: The sixth age shifts into the-and slipper'd pantaloon."('As You Like It')
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Jaques's Seven Ages of Man speech; the missing word describes the thin old man

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Seven Ages of Man speech with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed line has lost the missing word: the full line is 'into the lean and slipper'd pantaloon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective describes the thin, gaunt figure of old age in Shakespeare's speech.

clue.text: Use a ruler to reel in the fish

explanation.surface: Rule something off, or wind in the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight edge helps mark a straight stroke; an angler hauls in tackle when landing a catch.

clue.text: French banker invests nothing in Italian currency

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe, so the currency wraps round the zero

parts.note: lire were Italy's currency before the euro
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Paris financier puts no money into Italian lire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword trick: a river, which has banks; the Loire is France's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so in crossword terms it is a banker; this one flows through France.

clue.text: An energetic worker, but not a stayer

explanation.surface: A busy grafter who never sticks around.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is someone lively; a person who leaves or moves on is the opposite of one who remains.

clue.text: Suffer unusual danger in a riotous assembly

parts.note: to bear is to endure or suffer

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of danger are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Putting up with strange peril at a rowdy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a pit for bear-baiting, the term came to mean any scene of uproar.
